requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: openssl generated a 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed X.509 cert with CA:TRUE basicConstraints, subject/issuer CN=OS Comparison Root CA, O=OS Comparison Lab, valid 2026-2036, stored under /root/ca/oscomparison-root-ca.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Cert copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/, update-ca-trust extract run; trust list confirms it as an anchor, ca-bundle.crt contains it, and a leaf cert signed by the CA verifies via system trust with no explicit CAfile argument (implicit system trust), and again explicitly post-restart with -CAfile pointing at the system bundle.

requirements.requirement: CA trust anchor and functional verification survive a node restart (provider-wide restart protocol, independent of public contract but assessed per instructions)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured (boot_id 21de1f79..., system running, anchor present). Reboot triggered and acknowledged, node went unreachable (timeout, then reset), came back with a new boot_id (2655d3c4..., uptime=5s). Post-restart check shows system running, trust anchor still present in trust list and ca-bundle.crt, and the leaf cert still verifies against the system bundle — a full pre/disruption/post transition is directly observed.

overall_summary: The executor created the 'OS Comparison Root CA' self-signed root CA on node1 and installed it into the system trust store via update-ca-trust, with direct evidence (trust list, ca-bundle.crt content, and a leaf-cert verification against system trust) confirming it functions as a trusted CA. The mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and directly demonstrated: pre-restart healthy baseline, reboot acknowledgement, observed unreachability, a new boot_id post-restart, and confirmed persistence of both the CA trust anchor and functional verification after recovery.
limitations: Executor evidence for the restart protocol is self-selected; independently, only boot-identity global observations (before_prepare and after_executor) are available as a cross-check, and they corroborate the boot_id change but do not independently re-verify CA trust survival — that rests on the executor's own post-restart command.

No global observation set exists between before_prepare and after_prepare (alias/no-op since prepare was disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the executor_comparison diff, which shows only expected reboot-related churn (boot id, temp files, socket PIDs).

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (CA key/cert generation, anchor install, update-ca-trust extract, leaf cert generation for verification, reboot trigger) are directly tied to the task outcome or the mandated restart-evidence protocol. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, no package-state damage; listening sockets and failed-services lists are identical before/after aside from expected chronyd/sshd PID churn from the reboot. Minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log (from the backgrounded reboot command) and the CA/leaf key material under /root/ca/oscomparison-root-ca remain on disk after the run, but both are low-risk, bounded artifacts directly supporting the task's created CA and its verification — not unrelated experimentation.
